reconstructed_theorem_text: For every natural number n, including n = 0, there exists exactly one Borel measure mu on the full real orthogonal group O(n) = {A in R^(n x n) : A^T A = I} which has total mass one and is a Haar measure: it is invariant under left multiplication, finite on compact sets, and positive on every nonempty open set. O(n) carries its inherited finite real matrix topology and its Borel sigma-algebra; there is no determinant-one restriction.
objects: The full real orthogonal group O(n), and a Borel measure mu on that group. Haar means left invariant, finite on compact sets, and positive on nonempty open sets; probability means total mass one.
domains: n ranges over all natural numbers, including zero. Matrices have real entries indexed by Fin n in each coordinate. O(n) has the inherited finite real matrix topology and Borel sigma-algebra; O(0) is a singleton. No determinant-one restriction is imposed.
quantifiers: For every n, there exists exactly one measure mu satisfying the conjunction IsProbabilityMeasure mu and mu.IsHaarMeasure. Uniqueness is among measures satisfying both properties, not among all Borel measures.
assumptions: No caller premises beyond n being a natural number. Compactness, nonemptiness, Hausdorffness and second countability of O(n) are supplied internally by the approved context.
conclusion: Existence and uniqueness of a probability Haar measure on O(n), where Haar includes left invariance, finiteness on compact sets, and positivity on nonempty open sets.
scopes: The existence and uniqueness are separately for each n on the entire O(n), including n = 0. The statement does not identify the unique measure with a displayed constructor and does not separately assert right invariance or a sampling algorithm.
constant_dependencies: There are no free numerical constants. The uniquely specified measure depends on n and on the fixed group topology and Borel measurable structure; total mass is fixed at one.
